newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh PM vows to push through oil privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh PM vows to push through oil privatisation.

text.p: Kazakhstan's embattled prime minister vowed to push through privatisation of the Central Asian state's multi-billion dollar oil sector, the official daily Kazakhstanskaya Pravda said on Wednesday.
"The government intends to continue the privatisation process in all branches of industry, including the oil and gas sector," the daily quoted Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin as saying.
Kazhegeldin said the creation of state oil company Kazakh Oil to replace the country's oil and gas ministry "does not mean the suspension of privatisation in this (oil) sector".

He said Kazakh Oil would manage state-owned shares in joint ventures with foreign oil companies. Kazhegeldin's press service told the paper that the assets could later be sold off to develop the national securities market.

Some observers say the creation of Kazakh Oil is a setback for Kazhegeldin, whom President Nursultan Nazarbayev threatened to fire last week, as real control over oil sell-offs will pass to the head of Kazakh Oil, former oil and gas minister Nurlan Balgimbayev.
Results of a tender to sell off Kazakhstan's largest oil production concern, Mangistaumunaigaz, could be known on Friday.
